Roy Lichtenstein: Like New-Whitney Museu.name: Roy Lichtenstein: Like New
Roy Lichtenstein: Like New-Whitney Museu.description: Roy Lichtenstein’s breakthrough Pop work stunned both the art world and the country when it was first shown in the early 1960s. An appropriation artist long before the term was used by art historians, Lichtenstein took his imagery from comic books and newspapers, reconfiguring and refining his compositions before enlarging and transferring them to canvas.

Coumba Samba: Stars and Stripes-Whitney.name: Coumba Samba: Stars and Stripes
Coumba Samba: Stars and Stripes-Whitney.description: Coumba Samba’s installations draw on forms from the global built environment to expose the social, political, and economic structures they represent. In Stars and Stripes, Samba (b. 2000) uses the geometric shapes and bold colors of modernist abstraction to explore the entanglement of resource extraction with systems of power.

Roy Lichtenstein: 1997-Whitney Museum of.name: Roy Lichtenstein: 1997
Roy Lichtenstein: 1997-Whitney Museum of.description: Roy Lichtenstein: 1997 is presented on the Museum’s 3rd floor. This exhibition runs in conjunction with the major exhibition Roy Lichtenstein: Like New, opening October 11 on the Museum’s 5th floor. In 1997, at the age of seventy-three, Roy Lichtenstein (1923–1997) was as innovative and productive as ever. In addition to his studio painting practice, he was working on a variety of adventurous projects, among them two mural commissions, several large-scale sculptures, and a new series of prints.

The Lost World: The Art of Minnie Evans-.name: The Lost World: The Art of Minnie Evans
The Lost World: The Art of Minnie Evans-.description: Inspired by vivid dreams and visions, Minnie Evans (1892–1987) made her first drawing in 1935 after the death of her beloved grandmother. During the subsequent decades, the artist created hundreds of radiant pencil and crayon drawings, oil paintings, and collages that combined imagery from her Afro-Caribbean heritage, mythology, religion, popular culture, decorative arts, and the natural environment of her native Wilmington, North Carolina.

artport: A History of Internet Art-Whitn.name: artport: A History of Internet Art
artport: A History of Internet Art-Whitn.description: Screenshots from select projects commissioned by the Whitney Museum of American Art for its artport website. Image courtesy New Information artport: A History of Internet Art marks the twenty-fifth anniversary of artport, the Whitney’s online gallery space for commissions of net art, which launched in 2001. Since its inception, artport has presented a snapshot of the varied practices artists use to engage with an ever-evolving online environment.

Farah Al Qasimi: TAILSPIN-Whitney Museum.name: Farah Al Qasimi: TAILSPIN
Farah Al Qasimi: TAILSPIN-Whitney Museum.description: Farah Al Qasimi: TAILSPIN takes its title from the featured video work, TAILSPIN. Filmed in between Michigan, West Texas, and the East Coast, the work traces the long-standing relationship between American industry, oil, car culture, and Arab immigration. Told from the perspective of a jinn, or spirit, the work combines fictionalized storytelling, documentary-style footage, and real testimony to explore the complexities of identity-building in post-9/11 America.

Sonya Kelliher-Combs: TITIQ/MARK-Whitney.name: Sonya Kelliher-Combs: TITIQ/MARK
Sonya Kelliher-Combs: TITIQ/MARK-Whitney.description: Sonya Kelliher-Combs: TITIQ/MARK highlights nearly two decades of the artist’s explorations of history, cultural continuity, self-determination, and land use through her inventive approaches to artmaking. An Iñupiaq and Koyukon artist based in Anchorage, Alaska, Kelliher-Combs (b. 1969) makes paintings, sculptures, and installations that are deeply informed by generational knowledge.

Frank WANG Yefeng: The Levitating Perils.name: Frank WANG Yefeng: The Levitating Perils #2
Frank WANG Yefeng: The Levitating Perils.description: Frank WANG Yefeng’s The Levitating Perils #2 is a series of five animations that continues the artist’s explorations of identity and cultural displacement. The work features an uncanny, yet playful floating red dragon based on historical illustrations of the “Yellow Peril,” a label given to anti-Asian bias that dates back to the birth of European colonialism. The illustrations appeared in newspapers and political cartoons and featured monstrous depictions of Asian figures invading the West.

Alex Da Corte: Hot Dog With Ketchup-Whit.name: Alex Da Corte: Hot Dog With Ketchup

Taryn Simon: Father Country: I Do Love Y.name: Taryn Simon: Father Country: I Do Love You
Taryn Simon: Father Country: I Do Love Y.description: Experience an interactive installation by Taryn Simon featuring never-before-seen photographs, text, video, and sculpture.

Guggenheim Pop: 1960 to Now-Guggenheim M.name: Guggenheim Pop: 1960 to Now
Guggenheim Pop: 1960 to Now-Guggenheim M.description: From Andy Warhol to Maurizio Cattelan, this exhibition features Pop art from the collection and its enduring influence on contemporary artists.

Collection in Focus: Modern European Cur.name: Collection in Focus: Modern European Currents
Collection in Focus: Modern European Cur.description: See how artists like Natalia Goncharova, Vasily Kandinsky, and Franz Marc transformed painting in the early 20th century.

I dream in another language: Do Ho Suh-G.name: I dream in another language: Do Ho Suh
I dream in another language: Do Ho Suh-G.description: I dream in another language | Do Ho Suh will be the first major solo museum exhibition in New York dedicated to Korean artist Do Ho Suh (b. 1962, Seoul).

Tone-The Studio Museum in Harlem.name: Tone
Tone-The Studio Museum in Harlem.description: In drawings, paintings, photographs, and sculptures, the artists in Tone harness the expressive force of black, white, and every value between to demonstrate that tone functions beyond a technical condition as a unique material language.

Mark Bradford: Untitled (A\u2013Z), 2010.name: Mark Bradford: Untitled (A–Z), 2010
Mark Bradford: Untitled (A\u2013Z), 2010.description: Mark Bradford’s alphabet builds on an ongoing body of work called “merchant posters,” wherein the artist collects local business advertisements in his South Los Angeles neighborhood. Bradford layers and sands down these once-posted signs—featuring phrases such as “Stop Evictions” and “Affordable Daycare"—abstracting their original messaging so that only fragments remain. The result is twenty-six individual works on paper, each depicting a single letter from the English alphabet.

A sustained becoming: Studio Museum Arti.name: A sustained becoming: Studio Museum Artists in Residence 2026
A sustained becoming: Studio Museum Arti.description: A sustained becoming: Studio Museum Artists in Residence 2026 showcases the work of the Studio Museum in Harlem’s 2026 artists in residence, Derriann Pharr, Simonette Quamina, and Taylor Simmons, the first Artist-in-Residence cohort in the Museum’s new building.

Through Motion and Repose: Expanding the.name: Through Motion and Repose: Expanding the Walls 2026
Through Motion and Repose: Expanding the.description: Through Motion and Repose: Expanding the Walls 2026 features photography by the seventeen artists in this year’s cohort of the Studio Museum in Harlem’s signature teen program, Expanding the Walls: Making Connections Between Photography, History, and Community.

Geometries-The Studio Museum in Harlem.name: Geometries
Geometries-The Studio Museum in Harlem.description: Geometries centers the ancient mathematical study as a point of artistic inquiry, exploring how artists have used lines, shapes, and the spaces between to convey emotion, express identity, or work through formal concerns. Geometry helps us make sense of the world around us and the universe beyond. It works in tandem with our perception as we consider depth, volume, dimensionality, surface, measurement, distance, and structure.

Dreams of This Future: The Collection of.name: Dreams of This Future: The Collection of Peggy Cooper Cafritz
Dreams of This Future: The Collection of.description: This exhibition brings together a selection of works from a historic gift to the Studio Museum in Harlem by Peggy Cooper Cafritz (1947–2018) to celebrate her legacy as an advocate for the arts and her lifelong commitment to artists and their practices. An arts patron, educator, and civil rights activist, Cafritz bequeathed the majority of her art collection to the Studio Museum and the Duke Ellington School of the Arts, a public school in Washington, DC, which she cofounded in 1974.

Kapwani Kiwanga: BLEED-The Studio Museum.name: Kapwani Kiwanga: BLEED
Kapwani Kiwanga: BLEED-The Studio Museum.description: BLEED is a new site-specific commission by French and Canadian multimedia artist Kapwani Kiwanga. Installed in the Museum’s second-floor project gallery and on view from March 13, 2026, until April 1, 2027, BLEED draws inspiration from quilting traditions and the symbolism embedded in their intricate designs.

Woody De Othello: coming forth by day-Th.name: Woody De Othello: coming forth by day
Woody De Othello: coming forth by day-Th.description: Miami-born artist Woody De Othello’s solo presentation, coming forth by day, a new series of ceramic and wood sculptures, tiled wall works, and a large-scale bronze, travels to the Studio Museum in Harlem from the Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art, having originally been presented at the Pérez Art Museum Miami (PAMM). This will be the artist’s first institutional solo show in New York City.

Mavis Pusey: Mobile Images-The Studio Mu.name: Mavis Pusey: Mobile Images
Mavis Pusey: Mobile Images-The Studio Mu.description: Mavis Pusey: Mobile Images, coorganized by the Studio Museum in Harlem and the Institute of Contemporary Art at the University of Pennsylvania (ICA Philadelphia), marks the first major survey dedicated to the work and life of Jamaican-born artist Mavis Pusey (1928–2019), and features an array of artworks from Pusey's prolific fifty-year career.

Siena: The Art of Bronze, 1450\u20131500.name: Siena: The Art of Bronze, 1450–1500
Siena: The Art of Bronze, 1450\u20131500.description: Siena: The Art of Bronze, 1450–1500 is the first exhibition to focus on Siena as a center of artistic excellence and technical innovation in bronze sculpture during the Italian Renaissance. Bringing together some forty works—many of which have never been exhibited outside of Tuscany—the exhibition invites visitors to appreciate the medium’s beauty and versatility while learning about the complex

Kent Monkman: Officer and Laughing Girl-.name: Kent Monkman: Officer and Laughing Girl
Kent Monkman: Officer and Laughing Girl-.description: The Frick Collection will present an installation of new paintings by the contemporary artist Kent Monkman (b. Canada, 1965), whose practice explores historic European art and narratives from an Indigenous perspective. For this project, Monkman takes inspiration from Officer and Laughing Girl (ca. 1657)—one of the Frick’s three paintings by the seventeenth-century Dutch artist Johannes Vermeer—to

Painting with Fire: Susanne de Court and.name: Painting with Fire: Susanne de Court and the Art of Enamel
Painting with Fire: Susanne de Court and.description: The Frick Collection will present the first exhibition dedicated to the French enameler Susanne de Court. Active around 1600, De Court is an enigmatic figure in the creation of painted enamels. With nearly one hundred surviving works, she is widely believed to have been the only woman to lead a workshop in Limoges, France. This exhibition will bring together around forty-five of De Court’s signed

Vilhelm Hammersh\u00f8i: Pictures from H.name: Vilhelm Hammershøi: Pictures from Home
Vilhelm Hammersh\u00f8i: Pictures from H.description: The first major North American exhibition devoted to Vilhelm Hammershøi’s work in more than a decade, this show will focus on the artist’s most celebrated paintings—his series of enigmatic, evocative, and meticulously observed views of the interior of his apartment at Strandgade 30 in Copenhagen. Central themes of the show include the artist’s manipulation of spatial ambiguity; his handling of

Yoshitomo Nara-David Zwirner.name: Yoshitomo Nara
Yoshitomo Nara-David Zwirner.description: David Zwirner is pleased to present an exhibition by Japanese artist Yoshitomo Nara featuring new paintings and drawings, recent sculptures, and early works selected by the artist. Spanning the gallery's 537 West 20th Street and 533 West 19th Street locations in New York, this exhibition will be the artist's first solo presentation with David Zwirner and his first major solo exhibition in New York in nearly a decade.

Jem Perucchini: Sospiro-David Zwirner.name: Jem Perucchini: Sospiro
Jem Perucchini: Sospiro-David Zwirner.description: Explore Jem Perucchini: Sospiro at David Zwirner’s Tribeca location in New York, featuring new figurative paintings in the artist’s first US exhibition.

Li Hei Di: the year of mud-Pace Gallery.name: Li Hei Di: the year of mud
Li Hei Di: the year of mud-Pace Gallery.description: Pace will present “the year of mud,” an exhibition of new paintings by London-based artist Li Hei Di, at its 540 West 25th Street gallery from November 6 through December 19.

Lucas Samaras: Boxes and Reconstructions.name: Lucas Samaras: Boxes and Reconstructions
Lucas Samaras: Boxes and Reconstructions.description: “Lucas Samaras: Boxes and Reconstructions” will bring together two seminal bodies of work by the influential Greek-born American artist Lucas Samaras at Pace’s 540 West 25th Street gallery from November 6, 2026 through January 23, 2027

Elmgreen & Dragset: TRANSITION-Pace Gall.name: Elmgreen & Dragset: TRANSITION
Elmgreen & Dragset: TRANSITION-Pace Gall.description: Known for large-scale institutional transformations that fuse the typology of one space with another, Elmgreen & Dragset have explored how spatial design can communicate values and exercise control. In Transition, they direct their lens toward a site of political governance with their sculptural interpretation of the Oval Office.

David Byrne-Pace Gallery.name: David Byrne
David Byrne-Pace Gallery.description: Pace is pleased to present a special installation of drawings by artist David Byrne at its New York flagship. Drawn on the walls of the gallery’s stairwell landings between its first and seventh floors, these nine drawings reflect Byrne’s surreal and playful sensibility.Please note, this installation is currently closed while we install our upcoming exhibitions.

Gottlieb/Rothko: The Surrealist Years-Pa.name: Gottlieb/Rothko: The Surrealist Years
Gottlieb/Rothko: The Surrealist Years-Pa.description: 125 Newbury will present “Gottlieb/Rothko: The Surrealist Years,” an exhibition of paintings and works on paper by two of the central protagonists of Abstract Expressionism: Mark Rothko and Adolph Gottlieb.

Frederic Church in Jamaica-Cooper Hewitt.name: Frederic Church in Jamaica
Frederic Church in Jamaica-Cooper Hewitt.description: Frederic Church in Jamaica centers on the artist’s rarely exhibited sketches from his 1865 travels, presented within their historical context. The works document Jamaica’s plant life and landscapes in detailed observational studies.Celebrating the 200th anniversary of Frederic Church’s birth, this exhibition draws from Cooper Hewitt’s holdings of over 2,000 of the artists’ oil and graphite

The Substitute-Cooper Hewitt.name: The Substitute
The Substitute-Cooper Hewitt.description: Part of Design Across Time, Alexandra Daisy Ginsberg’s The Substitute is an immersive video and sound installation that digitally resurrects the extinct male Northern white rhino using artificial intelligence and state-of-the-art visual effects.

Sacred Splendor: Jewish Ritual Art and C.name: Sacred Splendor: Jewish Ritual Art and Christian Treasures from St. Vitus Cathedral in Prague
Sacred Splendor: Jewish Ritual Art and C.description: Sacred Splendor: Jewish Ritual Art and Christian Treasures from St. Vitus Cathedral in Prague brings Jewish and Christian sacred art from medieval to early modern Europe into dialogue, illuminating complex, interconnected histories across more than six centuries. The exhibition features Christian reliquaries on loan from St. Vitus Cathedral—the most extensive presentation of this treasury ever exhibited outside Europe—together with Jewish treasures never before shown in the United States.

Modernity and Opulence: Women of the Wie.name: Modernity and Opulence: Women of the Wiener Werkstätte
Modernity and Opulence: Women of the Wie.description: Modernity and Opulence: Women of the Wiener Werkstätte sheds new light on the role that Jewish women played as artists, designers, patrons, and tastemakers shaping modernist aesthetics in early 20 th -century Vienna and beyond.

Art in Focus: Oded Halahmy: Models in Wo.name: Art in Focus: Oded Halahmy: Models in Wood
Art in Focus: Oded Halahmy: Models in Wo.description: Oded Halahmy: Models in Wood presents sculptures made primarily in the 1970s, following Halahmy’s move to New York from London after studying at Saint Martin’s School of Art. Their titles evoke family, ritual, and spatial orientation, while their forms often suggest ladders and windows. Mostly made in advance of the artist’s monumental sculptures, each work is an intimate and hand-wrought expression of a singular artistic language rooted in memory and movement.

Art in Focus: Hannah Altman: Not a Circl.name: Art in Focus: Hannah Altman: Not a Circle but a Spiral
Art in Focus: Hannah Altman: Not a Circl.description: Vitus Cathedral in Prague Engaging with myth, performance, and memory—often through the lens of Jewish ritual and folklore—Hannah Altman’s photographs use everyday objects and scenery to conjure unexpectedly charged atmospheres.

Art in Focus: Afruz Amighi: Sounding She.name: Art in Focus: Afruz Amighi: Sounding Shell
Art in Focus: Afruz Amighi: Sounding She.description: Vitus Cathedral in Prague In the sculptural installation Sounding Shell, Afruz Amighi assembles a cast of mythological characters drawn from religions and cultures around the world. The Mexica goddess Coyolxāuhqui is a key figure: decapitated by her brother, according to myth, her severed head became the moon.

Art in Focus: Mordecai Ardon-The Jewish.name: Art in Focus: Mordecai Ardon
Art in Focus: Mordecai Ardon-The Jewish.description: Mordecai Ardon (1896–1992), born Mordecai Eliezer Bronstein, lived through multiple wars and harrowing events, including fleeing Nazi Germany in 1933. His triptych, Hiroshima – And there was Evening, and there was Morning ( Hiroshima—Il fut soir, il fut matin; 1988), grapples with the devastating magnitude of the nuclear bomb the United States unleashed on Hiroshima in 1945, during World War II. Created by the artist during the last years of his life, the work embodies his reflections on trauma.

Ruth Patir: (M)otherland-The Jewish Muse.name: Ruth Patir: (M)otherland
Ruth Patir: (M)otherland-The Jewish Muse.description: Originally created for the Israel Pavilion at the 2024 Venice Biennale, Ruth Patir’s multi-channel video work brings together ancient archaeology and contemporary digital technology to examine the intersection of gender, motherhood, and the fraught politics of fertility and reproductive rights.

Ma\u0142gorzata Mirga-Tas-The Jewish Mus.name: Małgorzata Mirga-Tas
Ma\u0142gorzata Mirga-Tas-The Jewish Mus.description: Małgorzata Mirga-Tas features artworks that memorialize and dignify victims and survivors of the Romani Holocaust, including such celebrated figures as the artist Ceija Stojka and the heroic Alfreda Noncia Markowska. It also debuts new work inspired by the history and experience of American Roma. A final chapter expands on the German Jewish art historian Aby Warburg’s pioneering study of iconology.

The Occupied City-Museum of the City of.name: The Occupied City
The Occupied City-Museum of the City of.venue: Museum of the City of New York
The Occupied City-Museum of the City of.description: Please note, the Tiffany gallery will be closed from 10 a.m.–12 p.m. on Tuesday, November 17. The exhibition will remain open to the public during this partial closure.Marking the 250th anniversary of the American Revolution, this major exhibition—developed in partnership with the Gotham Center for New York City History—transforms the Museum’s entire third floor into a 7,000-square-foot immersive journey through Revolutionary-era New York.

Halumii Ktapihna-Museum of the City of N.name: Halumii Ktapihna
Halumii Ktapihna-Museum of the City of N.venue: Museum of the City of New York
Halumii Ktapihna-Museum of the City of N.description: Bringing together the work of more than 30 artists alongside objects, archival materials, videos, and interactive listening stations, Halumii Ktapihna: Lenape Legacies and Futures invites visitors to encounter the enduring presence and living cultures of the Lenape/Lunáapeew—the original people of Lenapehoking/Lunaapeewáhkiing, the land now known as New York City and its surrounding region.

Gingerbread NYC-Museum of the City of Ne.name: Gingerbread NYC
Gingerbread NYC-Museum of the City of Ne.venue: Museum of the City of New York
Gingerbread NYC-Museum of the City of Ne.description: Discover a frosted wonderland in this annual wintertime tradition that invites bakers to recreate New York City icons out of gingerbread.

25th Anniversary Exhibition-Neue Galerie.name: 25th Anniversary Exhibition
25th Anniversary Exhibition-Neue Galerie.description: Organized in conjunction with the 25th anniversary of the founding of Neue Galerie New York, the exhibition fills the entirety of the museum's landmark building. Organized in conjunction with the 25th anniversary of the founding of Neue Galerie New York, the exhibition fills the entirety of the museum's landmark building.

Austrian Masterworks from the Neue Galer.name: Austrian Masterworks from the Neue Galerie
Austrian Masterworks from the Neue Galer.description: “Austrian Masterworks from the Neue Galerie” features highlights from the museum’s extensive collection of Austrian art from the period 1890 to 1940. Neue Galerie New York is the result of the close thirty-year friendship shared between art dealer and museum exhibition organizer Serge Sabarsky and Ronald S. Lauder, the museum’s co-founder and President. They spent countless hours together discussing Gustav Klimt, Egon Schiele, and Oskar Kokoschka.

1910: Portrait of a Year-Neue Galerie Ne.name: 1910: Portrait of a Year
1910: Portrait of a Year-Neue Galerie Ne.description: An investigation of Expressionism and New Classicism, two defining artistic currents. “1910: Portrait of a Year” investigates two defining artistic currents: Expressionism and New Classicism. These diametrically opposed impulses, one driven by ebullient hedonism, and the other by cerebral restraint, together shaped the major artistic achievements of the era. 1910 stands out as a pivotal year, when these contrasting impulses entered a dynamic and fertile dialogue.

No Ordinary Light: Akari at 75-The Noguc.name: No Ordinary Light: Akari at 75
No Ordinary Light: Akari at 75-The Noguc.description: Marking the 75th anniversary of Akari, this exhibition explores the enduring significance of Isamu Noguchi’s pioneering light sculptures. Isamu Noguchi created his first paper and bamboo light sculptures during a 1951 visit to Gifu that inspired him to reimagine the possibilities of traditional Japanese…

Isamu Noguchi at Lever House-The Noguchi.name: Isamu Noguchi at Lever House
Isamu Noguchi at Lever House-The Noguchi.description: Although the commission was never realized, the Lever House project became a defining moment in Noguchi’s career and established a lasting creative relationship between him and Bunshaft. The proposal crystallized ideas that would occupy Noguchi for decades: sculpture as landscape, public space as a…

Light and Stone: Revisiting Noguchi\u201.name: Light and Stone: Revisiting Noguchi’s 1986 Venice Biennale
Light and Stone: Revisiting Noguchi\u201.description: Additional works included large-scale stone and steel pieces as well as prominently featured Akari light sculptures. Noguchi included Akari despite strong reservations from Geldzahler and other close peers that their commercial associations would provoke criticism. The exhibition did not receive the…

Noguchi to Asawa: Designing Postwar Amer.name: Noguchi to Asawa: Designing Postwar America
Noguchi to Asawa: Designing Postwar Amer.description: Noguchi to Asawa: Designing Postwar America is the first exhibition of its kind to unite the work of six iconic artists: sculptor Isamu Noguchi (1904–1988), architect and furniture designer George Nakashima (1905–1990), sculptor Leo Amino (1911–1989), graphic designer S. Neil Fujita (1921–2010), fiber artist Kay Sekimachi (b. 1926), and sculptor Ruth Asawa (1926–2013).

Isamu Noguchi: \u201cI am not a designer.name: Isamu Noguchi: “I am not a designer”
Isamu Noguchi: \u201cI am not a designer.description: Isamu Noguchi: “I am not a designer,” organized by the High Museum of Art, is the first design retrospective of Isamu Noguchi’s work in nearly twenty-five years. Though Noguchi declared in 1949 “I am not a designer,” he regularly engaged with the space-shaping possibilities of design, imagining and producing work in architecture, industrial design, ceramics, furniture, lighting, stage sets, and landscape design.

Form, Shadow, Motion: Selections from th.name: Form, Shadow, Motion: Selections from the Burger Collection, Hong Kong
Form, Shadow, Motion: Selections from th.description: Continuing The Drawing Center’s tradition of exhibitions drawn from notable private collections, curator Olivia Shao has selected approximately fifty works on paper from the Burgers’ expansive holdings of more than 1,000 works on paper, to construct a focused visual essay on shared historical, poetic, and philosophical concerns, with Hong Kong and New York as twin points of reference and Eastern thought and Western philosophy as its guiding frameworks.

Nike: Form Follows Motion-Museum of Arts.name: Nike: Form Follows Motion
Nike: Form Follows Motion-Museum of Arts.description: The ultimate exhibition of the world’s most influential sports brand, Nike: Form Follows Motion traces Nike’s growth over the last five decades from a small Oregon running company into a global cultural force.

John Procario: Freeforms-Museum of Arts.name: John Procario: Freeforms
John Procario: Freeforms-Museum of Arts.description: John Procario: Freeforms highlights the contemporary designer’s sinuous ribbons of bentwood LED light sculptures and undulating furniture designs. To achieve the illusion of endless movement, Procario meticulously twists and shapes each strip of ash wood, which is then accentuated by discreetly embedded LEDs. Similarly, Procario’s Sculpted Sofas designs are completely informed by the shape and directionality of each work’s freeform wood base.

Jessica Lichtenstein: Rewilding-Museum o.name: Jessica Lichtenstein: Rewilding
Jessica Lichtenstein: Rewilding-Museum o.description: Jessica Lichtenstein: Rewilding transforms the Museum’s third-floor gallery into a lush, overgrown terrain, where thousands of digitally rendered female nudes coalesce into forests, ruins, and flowering canopies. A multidisciplinary artist whose practice spans large-scale installation, painting, sculpture, and video, Lichtenstein’s densely layered, technicolor landscapes are erotically charged, feminist reimaginings of nature and the female form.

Alice Riehl\u2019s Porcelain Florilegium.name: Alice Riehl’s Porcelain Florilegium
Alice Riehl\u2019s Porcelain Florilegium.description: This exhibition will be temporarily closed Oct 4 through 27 for the installation of a new wall mural. We apologize for any inconvenience.

I'm So Happy You Are Here: Japanese Wome.name: I'm So Happy You Are Here: Japanese Women Photographers from the 1950s to Now
I'm So Happy You Are Here: Japanese Wome.description: I’m So Happy You Are Here: Japanese Women Photographers from the 1950s to Now reconsiders and expands on the history of Japanese photography through the work twenty-eight intergenerational artists from the 1950s to today. Presented in partnership with Aperture and curated by Pauline Vermare, Lesley

Laia Abril: On Rape and Institutional Fa.name: Laia Abril: On Rape and Institutional Failure
Laia Abril: On Rape and Institutional Fa.description: In On Rape and Institutional Failure, an exhibition centered on the second chapter of her ongoing project A History of Misogyny, Laia Abril examines different forms of violence against women throughout history.Weaving together images, compiled testimonies, archival materials, select objects, and installations with sound and video, the exhibition investigates how gender-based stereotypes, coupled with worldwide prejudices and misconceptions, have contributed to a systemic rape culture that…

Saya Woolfalk: The WoodsWoman Method-The.name: Saya Woolfalk: The WoodsWoman Method
Saya Woolfalk: The WoodsWoman Method-The.venue: The Bronx Museum of the Arts
Saya Woolfalk: The WoodsWoman Method-The.description: As the first chapter of a multi-year initiative, Saya Woolfalk: The WoodsWoman Method presents process materials from artist Saya Woolfalk’s inaugural commission for The Bronx Museum’s renovated main lobby, opening in 2027, alongside related works from the Museum’s permanent collection.

Alex Strada: Public Address-The Bronx Mu.venue: The Bronx Museum of the Arts

Beyond the Margins: Bronx Museum Teens A.venue: The Bronx Museum of the Arts

Lifelong Studio Exhibition: Transcending.name: Lifelong Studio Exhibition: Transcending the Form—Abstract Figurative Painting
Lifelong Studio Exhibition: Transcending.venue: The Bronx Museum of the Arts

Locating Girlhood: Place and Identity in.name: Locating Girlhood: Place and Identity in Early American “Schoolgirl” Art
Locating Girlhood: Place and Identity in.description: Featuring spectacular examples of needlework and other ornamental arts made by American girls in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, Locating Girlhood: Place and Identity in Early American “Schoolgirl” Art sheds new light on a rich but understudied genre, offering one of the most significant presentations on the subject in recent memory.

Folk Nation: Crafting Patriotism in the.name: Folk Nation: Crafting Patriotism in the United States
Folk Nation: Crafting Patriotism in the.description: Mounted during the celebration of the United States semiquincentennial, Folk Nation: Crafting Patriotism in the United States draws from the American Folk Art Museum’s rich collections to explore links between vernacular art and the construction of an American sense of self.

There's no me without you-Pioneer Works.name: There's no me without you
There's no me without you-Pioneer Works.description: There's no me without you is an installation grounded in artist Finnegan Shannon’s longtime fantasy of an exhibition space that would meet their access...

Tuomas A. Laitinen: Siphon-Pioneer Works.name: Tuomas A. Laitinen: Siphon
Tuomas A. Laitinen: Siphon-Pioneer Works.description: Siphon, a multimedia installation created by Helsinki-based artist Tuomas A. Laitinen, draws on more than a decade of research in octopus intelligence,...

LaJun\u00e9 McMillian: Child/ren of the.name: LaJuné McMillian: Child/ren of the Bloom
LaJun\u00e9 McMillian: Child/ren of the.description: Child/ren of the Bloom by LaJuné McMillian is an interactive, multidisciplinary installation that explores the threshold between land and sea, and the b...

Johan Orellana: Remnants of Forking Path.name: Johan Orellana: Remnants of Forking Paths
Johan Orellana: Remnants of Forking Path.description: Remnants of Forking Paths considers migration as both a historical condition and an intimate, ongoing experience. Orellana uses photography, collage, and found materials to explore the Ecuadorian migrant experience that emerged in the late 1990s and early 2000s, following Ecuador’s economic crisis and a wave of migration to New York and Spain at large. The […]

From the BRIClab: Works from the 2025-26.name: From the BRIClab: Works from the 2025-26 Artist Residencies
From the BRIClab: Works from the 2025-26.description: This fall, BRIC will present an exhibition featuring new work by the 2025–2026 BRIClab Contemporary Art and Video Art artists-in-residence. Developed, seeded, or significantly expanded during their residencies, the exhibition highlights what becomes possible when artists are given sustained time, space, resources, and freedom to experiment. Working across painting, installation, photography, textiles, and video, the […]

Marc Hundley: SATELLITES ARE OUT TONIGHT.name: Marc Hundley: SATELLITES ARE OUT TONIGHT
Marc Hundley: SATELLITES ARE OUT TONIGHT.description: “As far as expressing myself a T-shirt works the best. A person wearing it is saying it. The shape of a T-shirt is the form of a person. It’s very simple and such a common object. It’s not original to put words on a T-shirt. It’s just a T-shirt, so it’s not criticized like art with a capital A. Anyone can make one themselves. The shirts give me a place I can get things off my chest. To then put them back on my chest.” – Marc Hundley

SHOP: Artists Who Do Shirts-White Column.name: SHOP: Artists Who Do Shirts
SHOP: Artists Who Do Shirts-White Column.description: On the occasion of Marc Hundley’s solo exhibition, White Columns is pleased to present Shop: Artists Who Do Shirts, a collection of artist-made t-shirts for purchase. Thank you for supporting White Columns. Click checkout below to complete your purchase via Shopify.

White Columns Online #38: Clothes, not F.description: White Columns is New York City’s oldest alternative non-profit space.

How We Work: Smack Mellon at 30-Smack Me.description: On the occasion of the organization’s 30th Anniversary, Smack Mellon presents a group exhibition reflecting on our work over the past three decades.

Steffani Jemison: Cant-The Kitchen.name: Steffani Jemison: Cant
Steffani Jemison: Cant-The Kitchen.description: Gallery hours: Wednesday–Saturday, 12–6pm (Free) | Performances: January 21, 28, and February 4, 2027, 7pm Tickets: Sliding scale; $10-30 The Kitchen presents Steffani Jemison: Cant (December 4, 2026–February 6, 2027). This solo presentation marks the artist’s debut at The Kitchen and her first institutional solo exhibition in New York City in nearly ten years.

Art of Manga-Brooklyn Museum.name: Art of Manga
Art of Manga-Brooklyn Museum.description: Art of Manga is the first major exhibition in the Americas to explore manga—Japanese comics and graphic novels—as an art form.

Iris van Herpen: Sculpting the Senses-Br.name: Iris van Herpen: Sculpting the Senses
Iris van Herpen: Sculpting the Senses-Br.description: Iris van Herpen: Sculpting the Senses celebrates one of the most forward-thinking fashion designers of her generation.

Breaking the Mold: Brooklyn Museum at 20.name: Breaking the Mold: Brooklyn Museum at 200
Breaking the Mold: Brooklyn Museum at 20.description: From groundbreaking early acquisitions to striking new additions, the Brooklyn Museum’s collection has always championed artists and artworks that catalyze imaginative storytelling and brave conversations. As we ring in our 200th anniversary, Breaking the Mold: Brooklyn Museum at 200 celebrates this unique legacy.

Donald Moffett: IMPEACH-Brooklyn Museum.name: Donald Moffett: IMPEACH
Donald Moffett: IMPEACH-Brooklyn Museum.description: Step onto the floor of the US House of Representatives in December 1998. As the chamber debates whether to impeach President Bill Clinton, Representative John Lewis delivers a deeply personal speech about surviving a devastating storm—and about holding a divided nation together. In IMPEACH, artist Donald Moffett (American, born 1955) turns that moment into an immersive sound installation, inviting listeners to hear Lewis’s words and their echoes anew.

C\u00e9zanne to Modigliani: Gifts of Mod.name: Cézanne to Modigliani: Gifts of Modern Art from the Pearlman Collection
C\u00e9zanne to Modigliani: Gifts of Mod.description: Discover more than 50 modern European masterpieces—representing one of the most important gifts of European art in the Brooklyn Museum’s history—and meet the remarkable collectors who brought them together.

Mika Ninagawa: Feel the Flow(ers)-Brookl.name: Mika Ninagawa: Feel the Flow(ers)
Mika Ninagawa: Feel the Flow(ers)-Brookl.description: Wander into a dreamlike, color-filled universe where you can touch, see, and feel the flow(ers). One of Japan’s most celebrated contemporary photographers, Mika Ninagawa (born 1972) creates portals to otherworldly realms.

Hopi Kachina Dolls: Blessings for a Bala.name: Hopi Kachina Dolls: Blessings for a Balanced World
Hopi Kachina Dolls: Blessings for a Bala.description: Kachina dolls (tithu) represent the Katsina spirits who bring much-needed rain and balance to the Hopi people of northeastern Arizona. Carved from cottonwood and distinctively designed, the dolls are treasured gifts from the spirits, given primarily to Hopi girls and women. This exhibition is the first to examine the Hopi kachina dolls tradition from their recipients’ perspective.

Rubin Museum Tibetan Buddhist Shrine Roo.name: Rubin Museum Tibetan Buddhist Shrine Room
Rubin Museum Tibetan Buddhist Shrine Roo.description: A lamplit sanctuary amid the bustle of Brooklyn—and a refuge in uncertain times—the Rubin Museum Tibetan Buddhist Shrine Room is a place to learn, reflect, and seek inspiration.

Mike Kelley: Jerry Meandering-Hauser & W.name: Mike Kelley: Jerry Meandering
Mike Kelley: Jerry Meandering-Hauser & W.description: This November, in collaboration with the Mike Kelley Foundation for the Arts, Hauser & Wirth will present ‘Mike Kelley: Jerry Meandering,’ an exhibition focused on the artist’s works on paper, some of which will be shown publicly for the first time.

Harmony Korine: UX LAM-Hauser & Wirth.name: Harmony Korine: UX LAM
Harmony Korine: UX LAM-Hauser & Wirth.description: Harmony Korine has developed a wide-ranging practice over the last three decades that spans film, painting, sculpture and fashion, all unified by a distinctive combination of improvisation, humor, repetition, nostalgia and poetry. Moving freely between mediums, Korine continually invents imaginative new visual languages that resist easy categorization. Across his varied oeuvre, each body of work unfolds with its own formal and emotional lexicon.

Zeng Fanzhi-Hauser & Wirth.name: Zeng Fanzhi
Zeng Fanzhi-Hauser & Wirth.description: For his first New York City exhibition in over a decade, Zeng Fanzhi will present a new sculpture and a suite of resplendent new paintings that conjure imagined celestial landscapes and topographies. The works advance the celebrated Beijing-based artist’s ongoing investigation of color, perception and the material possibilities of paint.

Cristina Iglesias: Possible Matter-Hause.name: Cristina Iglesias: Possible Matter
Cristina Iglesias: Possible Matter-Hause.description: For ‘Possible Matter,’ her first New York exhibition with the gallery, Spanish artist Cristina Iglesias will debut a new immersive dome installation alongside four wall-based sculptures from her new ‘Possible Matter’ series, exploring the shifting boundaries between the built and natural worlds.

Rashid Johnson: Birthday Boys-Hauser & W.name: Rashid Johnson: Birthday Boys
Rashid Johnson: Birthday Boys-Hauser & W.description: This November, Rashid Johnson will present an exhibition of new work that considers the complex relationship between fathers and sons.

Lari Pittman: The Remedy of Analog Space.name: Lari Pittman: The Remedy of Analog Space and Time
Lari Pittman: The Remedy of Analog Space.description: Lehmann Maupin is pleased to present Lari Pittman’s solo exhibition The Remedy of Analog Space and Time, unveiling a new body of work by the Los Angeles-based painter featuring ten new paintings. Few living artists have shaped the language of contemporary painting as profoundly as Pittman.

Leonora Carrington & Cecilia Vicu\u00f1a.name: Leonora Carrington & Cecilia Vicuña
Leonora Carrington & Cecilia Vicu\u00f1a.description: Lehmann Maupin and Gallery Wendi Norris are pleased to announce Leonora Carrington & Cecilia Vicuña, an exhibition placing the work of these two pioneering artists into dialogue for the first time. This two-part exhibition will open at Lehmann Maupin in New York on November 19, before traveling to Gallery Wendi Norris in San Francisco in January 2027.

Nairy Baghramian: nameless-Marian Goodma.name: Nairy Baghramian: nameless
Nairy Baghramian: nameless-Marian Goodma.description: Marian Goodman Gallery is pleased to present a solo exhibition by Nairy Baghramian. On view are recent works, which were first presented in an exhibition at WIELS, Belgium in late 2025 and that will be shown in the United States for the first time.

Claes Oldenburg: Six Themes-Paula Cooper.name: Claes Oldenburg: Six Themes
Claes Oldenburg: Six Themes-Paula Cooper.description: The Estate of Claes Oldenburg & Coosje van Bruggen and Paula Cooper Gallery, New York, will present a major exhibition of sculpture, drawings and prints by Claes Oldenburg in the Fall of 2026.

Art is for the Spirit: Records of the Se.name: Art is for the Spirit: Records of the Self
Art is for the Spirit: Records of the Se.description: Art is the only way to run away without leaving home – Twyla Tharp[1] Paula Cooper Gallery is pleased to present Art is for the Spirit: Records of the Self, a group exhibition organized by Ivy Shapiro with work by Jennifer Bartlett, Jonathan Borofsky, Robert Gober, David Hammons, Kazuko Miyamoto, Ree Morton, Elizabeth Murray, and Joel Shapiro. The exhibition gathers work that explores the home and autobiography as tools for grounding the self.

Kehinde Wiley: What the Light Becomes-Se.name: Kehinde Wiley: What the Light Becomes
Kehinde Wiley: What the Light Becomes-Se.description: Sean Kelly Gallery is delighted to announce, What the Light Becomes, Kehinde Wiley’s fourth exhibition at the gallery. The exhibition focuses specifically on contemporary New Yorkers and, more broadly, on how New York represents a portrait of America at this moment, not as a single cohesive identity, but as something diverse, shifting and continually being remade.

Tschabalala Self: Tools of Worship-Petze.name: Tschabalala Self: Tools of Worship
Tschabalala Self: Tools of Worship-Petze.description: Petzel is pleased to present Tools of Worship, Tschabalala Self ’s ﬁrst solo exhibition with the gallery and her ﬁrst gallery exhibition in New York since 2020. The show brings together new paintings and the artist’s ﬁrst sculptural works in concrete.

James Little: Homage El Shabazz-Petzel G.name: James Little: Homage El Shabazz
James Little: Homage El Shabazz-Petzel G.description: Petzel is pleased to present Homage El Shabazz, James Little’s third exhibition with the gallery, which brings together a rarely seen body of work from a pivotal moment in Little’s practice. The exhibition comprises six intimately scaled paintings from Little’s Homage El Shabazz series made between 1985 and 1989. This show marks the largest presentation of the series since 1992, when six of these works were included in the Walker Art Center’s Malcom X: Man, Ideal, Icon exhibition curated by Dr.

Jason Moran: Stacks-Luhring Augustine.name: Jason Moran: Stacks
Jason Moran: Stacks-Luhring Augustine.description: Luhring Augustine is pleased to announce STACKS, an exhibition of new and recent work by Jason Moran, will open on November 6 and remain on view through December 19. Marking the artist's third solo show with the gallery, the presentation continues Moran's inquiry into the histories, objects, gestures, and ideas that shape jazz and its cultural landscape, explored through a range of materials including works on paper, sculpture, and video.

Inka Essenhigh-Miles McEnery Gallery.name: Inka Essenhigh
Inka Essenhigh-Miles McEnery Gallery.description: Miles McEnery Gallery presents its fourth Inka Essenhigh exhibition exploring landscapes, organic forms, and the shifting boundaries between the natural and imagined worlds. Her distinctive visual language transforms everyday environments into otherworldly scenes filled with mystery, movement, and wonder. Through her exploration of floral motifs, fauna, and still lifes, Essenhigh’s paintings teeter on the edge of reality before breaking through into vibrant, dreamlike landscapes.

Karel Funk-Miles McEnery Gallery.name: Karel Funk
Karel Funk-Miles McEnery Gallery.description: Karel Funk’s inaugural solo exhibition at Miles McEnery Gallery continues his exploration of the hood as a contemporary form of portraiture, shifting focus away from the individual beneath the garment and toward an investigation of the materiality of the garment itself. Through intricate detail and iridescent color, the works explore the interplay of figuration, abstraction, geometry, and perception. Funk’s figures dwell in the ambiguous space between the seen and unseen.

Natural Order-Miles McEnery Gallery.name: Natural Order
Natural Order-Miles McEnery Gallery.description: Miles McEnery Gallery is pleased to announce a curated group exhibition titled Natural Order, featuring a selection of works by artists Karin Davie, Lisa Corinne Davis, Douglas Melini, Alexander Ross, and James Siena. This exhibition explores the system of rules, patterns, and relationships that dictate the physical universe independently of human design.

Daniel Rich-Miles McEnery Gallery.name: Daniel Rich
Daniel Rich-Miles McEnery Gallery.description: Daniel Rich presents a new body of paintings in his exhibition Magic Mountain, examining themes of political power, memory, and history through nocturnal scenes of New York City. Towering buildings in rich colors of sapphire blue, amethyst purple, and tangerine fill Rich’s cityscapes with anticipation, silence, and a subtle tension suggested by an unseen activity or emptiness within.

Eric Fischl: In Pursuit of Pleasure-Skar.name: Eric Fischl: In Pursuit of Pleasure

Steve Locke: I said what I said-Alexande.name: Steve Locke: I said what I said
Steve Locke: I said what I said-Alexande.description: Alexander Gray Associates presents Steve Locke: I said what I said, an exhibition of recent paintings, sculptures, and neon. Returning to questions of sexuality and desire, racial violence, the politics of looking, and the conventions of portraiture and modernism, the exhibition brings together lines of inquiry Locke has sustained...

Ellen Gronemeyer: D\u00c9J\u00c0 VU-Anto.name: Ellen Gronemeyer: DÉJÀ VU
Ellen Gronemeyer: D\u00c9J\u00c0 VU-Anto.description: Anton Kern Gallery is pleased to announce Ellen Gronemeyer’s third solo exhibition in New York. For DÉJÀ VU, the Berlin-based artist presents twelve new oil paintings and, for the first time, five small tables. Positioning the imaginary space of a painting alongside functional objects, the exhibition considers the act...

Pawe\u0142 Althamer: Artist/Studio-Anton.name: Paweł Althamer: Artist/Studio
Pawe\u0142 Althamer: Artist/Studio-Anton.description: Anton Kern Gallery is pleased to announce Artist/Studio, an exhibition of new work by Paweł Althamer. This is his second exhibition at the gallery and his third in New York, following The Neighbors at the New Museum in 2014. For Artist/Studio, Althamer will move his studio from Warsaw...

Elodie Blanchard: In Fragments-Jane Lomb.name: Elodie Blanchard: In Fragments
Elodie Blanchard: In Fragments-Jane Lomb.description: Jane Lombard Gallery is pleased to present In Fragments, a solo exhibition of work by Elodie Blanchard. Bringing together three ongoing series, Trees, Mending Joy, and Vessels, the exhibition explores Blanchard’s longstanding engagement with textiles as a medium for transformation. Drawing from collected fabrics, clothing, Mylar balloons, and...

Rachael Catharine Anderson: Hidden Peril.name: Rachael Catharine Anderson: Hidden Peril
Rachael Catharine Anderson: Hidden Peril.description: Jane Lombard Gallery is pleased to present Hidden Peril, a new body of paintings by Rachael Catharine Anderson centered on poisonous plants and mushrooms. Continuing her longstanding practice of painting botanical subjects from direct observation, Anderson turns her attention to the shadow side of the natural world, where beauty...

John Baeder: America-ACA Galleries.name: John Baeder: America
John Baeder: America-ACA Galleries.description: New York, NY — ACA Galleries is pleased to announce John Baeder's second solo exhibition at the gallery in collaboration with MB Abram. The show includes paintings from Baeder's personal collection, including his final series of matchbook covers completed in 2018.

Scott Lyall: Reds-Miguel Abreu Gallery.name: Scott Lyall: Reds
Scott Lyall: Reds-Miguel Abreu Gallery.description: There may be light of different wavelengths independent of observers (such as infrared), but there is no color without observers. Miguel Abreu Gallery is pleased to announce the opening, on Friday, November 6, of Scott Lyall’s REDS, his seventh one-person exhibition at the gallery. The show is comprised of what appear as six monochrome inkjet paintings along with four small glass works.

Jimmy Raskin\u2019s Curio Shop-Miguel Ab.name: Jimmy Raskin’s Curio Shop
Jimmy Raskin\u2019s Curio Shop-Miguel Ab.description: Miguel Abreu Gallery is pleased to announce the opening, on Friday, November 6, of Jimmy Raskin’s Curio Shop, his sixth one-person exhibition at the gallery. Jimmy Raskin was a poet. At the age of nineteen, however, Raskin stopped writing poetry to devote himself to exploring and manifesting the conditions under which what he calls ‘the Poem’ might remain an achievable aim in our current cultural conditions.

Rebecca Morris: #35-Bortolami.name: Rebecca Morris: #35
Rebecca Morris: #35-Bortolami.description: Bortolami is pleased to announce Rebecca Morris’ third exhibition with the gallery and her thirty-fifth solo exhibition to date. Morris continues to probe the vast range of oil paint’s material possibilities, drawing on decades of experimentation with thin, aqueous color to push the boundaries of contemporary painting.

As a moment and as an accumulation: Maki.name: As a moment and as an accumulation: Maki Katayama, Hikari Ono
As a moment and as an accumulation: Maki.description: Bortolami is pleased to present a two-person exhibition of works by Maki Katayama and Hikari Ono in The Upstairs, organized by Richard Aldrich. While working in distinct mediums—from Katayama’s systematic exploration of color classification on canvas to Ono’s wall sculptures, characterized by their meticulously treated surfaces—both artists approach painting as a conceptual framework rather than a set of techniques.

Karon Davis: Wishful Thinking-Salon 94.name: Karon Davis: Wishful Thinking
Karon Davis: Wishful Thinking-Salon 94.description: Wishful Thinking is Karon Davis’ meditation on the complicated, all too often absent role of the Black figure within the canon of art history. The exhibition presents new life-size, nude sculptures created from body casting friends, muses, and models. Incorporating and expanding upon the classical tradition of sculpture, Davis reconsiders the nude through a contemporary lens.

Ludovic Nkoth: Between Lines-Salon 94.name: Ludovic Nkoth: Between Lines
Ludovic Nkoth: Between Lines-Salon 94.description: Meaning is invisible, but the invisible is not the contradictory of the visible: the visible itself has an invisible inner framework. – Maurice Merleau-Ponty in The Visible and the Invisible For Ludovic Nkoth, the body is never simply what appears on its surface. A gesture, a posture, a face, or a painted line can reveal something while leaving something else just beyond view.

Tuan Andrew Nguyen: Sacred Forest / R\u0.name: Tuan Andrew Nguyen: Sacred Forest / Rù'ng Thiêng
Tuan Andrew Nguyen: Sacred Forest / R\u0.description: Norr Cohan is pleased to present an exhibition of new work by Tuan Andrew Nguyen, on view from October 30 through December 19, 2026, at the gallery’s 48 and 52 Walker Street locations. For the artist’s fourth solo exhibition at the gallery, Nguyen brings together his expansive film oeuvre with his long-standing sculptural practice of transforming material remnants of war into objects of healing.

Mildred Thompson: Cosmos Calling-Galerie.name: Mildred Thompson: Cosmos Calling
Mildred Thompson: Cosmos Calling-Galerie.description: Galerie Lelong, New York, is pleased to announce an upcoming exhibition of work by Mildred Thompson (b. 1936-d. 2003), the gallery's third exhibition dedicated to the groundbreaking American artist. Entitled Cosmos Calling, the exhibition presents her masterwork Music of the Spheres paintings alongside a selection from her Heliocentric Series.

Friends and Legends: The Collection of M.name: Friends and Legends: The Collection of Michael Chow

Brice Marden: I Am Plane Image-Gagosian.name: Brice Marden: I Am Plane Image

Doom Drop-Museum of the Moving Image.name: Doom Drop
Doom Drop-Museum of the Moving Image.description: Doom Drop , an independent video game by Dexter Gramfors in a custom arcade cabinet, is free to play in the Museum lobby.

nephomancer-Museum of the Moving Image.name: nephomancer
nephomancer-Museum of the Moving Image.description: In this new commission for the Schlosser Media Wall, misha de ridder (b. 1971, Netherlands) and miragenesi (b. 1986, Italy) connect photographic evidence with nephomancy, the practice of reading clouds for signs and predictions.

It\u2019s a Dream (2007)-Museum of the M.name: It’s a Dream (2007)
It\u2019s a Dream (2007)-Museum of the M.description: In 2007, the Cannes Film Festival invited Tsai Ming-liang and more than 30 other directors to make three-minute films about the experience of going to the movies. Tsai responded with It’s a Dream , drawing on memories of the cinemas he attended as a child in Malaysia. On view in the Jane Henson Amphitheater through November 29.

Seeing the Cinema: Photographic Visions.name: Seeing the Cinema: Photographic Visions of Movie Theaters
Seeing the Cinema: Photographic Visions.description: This exhibition explores the movie theater as both architectural icon and cultural form through a range of photographic practices, offering a powerful meditation on what it has meant—and continues to mean—to gather in the dark to watch stories unfold on a screen.

Felix the Cat-Museum of the Moving Image.name: Felix the Cat
Felix the Cat-Museum of the Moving Image.description: MoMI presents four restored Felix the Cat cartoons from 1927–28. Watch Felix travel to the bottom of the sea to source a string of pearls (only to be chased out by the angry mother oyster), fashion a straw out of a yard of stolen pasta, attempt to court Juliet (as Romeow) while dueling another suitor and a group of musical animals, and, after a failed outing to the cinema, make his own movie,

Site Interruptions-Museum of the Moving.name: Site Interruptions
Site Interruptions-Museum of the Moving.description: Site Interruptions is a new series of artist commissions unfolding across MoMI’s homepage and unexpected locations in the Museum’s building.

Overexposed: Art, Technology, and the Bo.name: Overexposed: Art, Technology, and the Body
Overexposed: Art, Technology, and the Bo.description: Major new exhibition exploring how cinema and X-ray technology radically transformed how we see and understand the human form through the work of 16 artists and decades of research films

Buddha and Shiva, Lotus and Dragon-Asia.name: Buddha and Shiva, Lotus and Dragon
Buddha and Shiva, Lotus and Dragon-Asia.description: This exhibition celebrates Asia Society's 70th anniversary with 70 of the finest works from the permanent collection.

Blanchette Hooker Rockefeller-Asia Socie.name: Blanchette Hooker Rockefeller
Blanchette Hooker Rockefeller-Asia Socie.description: Blanchette Hooker Rockefeller was an active partner in the creation of Asia Society's Museum and permanent collection.

A Legacy Continued: Recent Acquisitions-.name: A Legacy Continued: Recent Acquisitions
A Legacy Continued: Recent Acquisitions-.description: As part of our 70th anniversary celebration, this exhibition features recent gifts from Rockefeller family members.

Busy, Busy Towns-Asia Society Museum.name: Busy, Busy Towns
Busy, Busy Towns-Asia Society Museum.description: These video works explore how rapidly evolving cultural, political, and ecological issues have shaped urban landscapes across contemporary Asia, and in particular China, Indonesia, and Taiwan.
